Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In a directed graph G(V, E) stored via an adjacency list, the operation on vertex v incurs a cost equal to the out-degree of v, meaning the number of outgoing edges from that vertex. To find the worst-case single operation cost and the aggregate amortized cost, we examine the maximum possible out-degree of any vertex and the sum of all out-degrees across the entire sequence of |V| operations.

* (a) The cost of the worst possible single operation is |V| − 1, which is achieved when a particular vertex has a directed edge to every other vertex in the graph, giving it the maximum possible out-degree in a simple directed graph.
* (b) The average amortized cost under aggregate analysis is |E| / |V|, because the total cost over all |V| operations equals the sum of out-degrees of every vertex, which is exactly the total number of edges |E|, and dividing by the number of operations (|V|) yields the per-operation amortized cost.
